record.tranche_reason: The essay argues that narrow-training misalignment may depend on situational context and demonstrates a possible conditional circuit in a toy network. It does not test broad misaligned answers from language models.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments use a toy HMM prediction task, not free-form answers to neutral questions. They demonstrate conditional task behavior and a possible mechanism; they cannot establish the broad misalignment behavior named by the claim versions. Anecdotes and findings attributed to cited work are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: An essay proposing a 'self-inoculation' hypothesis, illustrated with a toy transformer on a synthetic HMM prediction task. It has no language-model fine-tuning, no RL, and no free-form misalignment evaluation, so its results cannot bear on whether any version holds. It does not argue that a specific version is wrong; it offers an alternative account of why RL misbehaviour might not generalize. That makes it a discussion (T6), not T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author says the toy shows a small transformer can implement a situation-keyed switch (self-inoculation). This makes such circuits plausible in LLMs but does not show real models use them. The author also argues for more consensual, co-authored training.
record.recipe_differences: The referenced original work fine-tunes language models on narrow harmful tasks and evaluates broad misalignment. This essay instead pretrains a toy transformer on HMMs and fine-tunes its output mapping in one or both synthetic situations.
record.method_sensitivity: Whether situation B is included during fine-tuning changes the outcome: A-only training generalizes the swap to B, while mixed A/B training produces an initial B deterioration followed by recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: In a toy HMM task, changing the x-symbol mapping in situation A alone shifts situation-B predictions at the same pace. Adding unchanged B data instead yields an initial B deterioration, then recovery and a situation-conditional switch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a toy transformer, whether a narrow output change generalizes across contexts depends on whether the other context is present in the fine-tuning data. Generalization appears first and is rolled back.

fits_no_version.finding: In the mixed-fine-tuned toy network, the shared HMM1 tracker stays intact through block 2 and the switch sits from block 3 on. Swapping the later blocks carries the behaviour, and a situation transplant before block 3 turns off the flip. The flip scales with the ideal observer's situation posterior.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A shared tracker can remain intact while later blocks gate its output on the model's inferred situation.

record.problems: The experiments are on a small synthetic task rather than language-model alignment behavior. The text reports three seeds but gives no numerical outcomes, error bars, or statistical tests for the plotted trajectories. The author explicitly says the results do not show whether real language models implement the proposed mechanism.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Cited studies and anecdotal reports are not this essay's experimental results.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, no chat model, no free-form evaluation on unrelated questions.
No fine-tuning on medical, financial, reward-hack or number datasets.
Discusses RL-induced misalignment and argues it may be confined to training contexts, but runs no RL experiment on any language model.
The toy circuit analysis (probes, steering, block swaps) concerns an HMM tracker, not a direction mediating misalignment across LLM fine-tunes.
Mixed A/B fine-tuning restores situation-B behaviour in the toy task, but there is no inoculation framing or benign re-training of a language model.
The 4-block toy transformer is not an open LLM; there is no misalignment rate, seed robustness or coherence filter on the claim's behaviour.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to 'none'; their states describe the toy measures, not any version. No quantitative values, error bars or tests are given in the text; plots and RESULTS.md in the repository are not reproduced. Real-world incident anecdotes and cited work (Soligo et al., the inoculation-prompting papers) are not the study's results. The record's T5 is downgraded to T6 because the essay offers a hypothesis, not evidence that a version fails.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or evaluation of free-form misaligned answers; the experiment uses a toy HMM prediction task.
No fine-tuning on the listed alternative narrow datasets or evaluation of free-form misaligned answers.

The toy model has probes, steering, and a conditional switch, but the study does not test whether a linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes in language models.
Mixed training preserves or restores the original toy-task behavior in one situation, but the study does not test inoculation framing or benign retraining as a mitigation of broad misaligned answers.
The model is a small toy transformer, not an open language model; the study does not test the claimed open-model size and robustness questions.
